clue.text: Insurance for Lib Dems?

definitions.meaning: cover against claims from other people, the legal minimum for a British motorist
the Liberal Democrats long sat behind Labour and the Conservatives as Britain's third force in politics

explanation.surface: A question about what cover a political party might take out.
explanation.walkthrough: The Liberal Democrats are a UK political party, traditionally the third largest after Labour and the Conservatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Motor policies covering only damage to others are called this, and the same phrase names the Lib Dems' political ranking.

clue.text: Mike secretly tackling the Italian racket in construction

indicators.note: taking on, so the bugging word grips the next pieces inside it

parts.note: to mike someone secretly is to bug them, plant a hidden microphone
il is Italian for 'the'
a din is a racket, a loud noise

explanation.surface: Someone covertly recording an Italian construction racket, a mafia-style scam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mike' is not the NATO letter M but a verb, to put a microphone on.
explanation.definitionFit: A construction is an erected structure, a synonym for an edifice.

clue.text: Bond writer comes into a little money

indicators.note: enters, so the writer's word sits inside the coin

parts.note: a cent is a small coin
the setter refers to themself as 'me'

explanation.surface: A Bond author receives a modest windfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests James Bond and his writer, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cement binds materials together, as a noun or verb it is a synonym for glue or adhesive bond.

clue.text: Lost boring game? That's old hat

indicators.note: drilling into, so the abbreviation goes inside the match word

parts.note: a tie is a match, as in a cup tie
L is the abbreviation for lost in a table of results

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses losing a match as stale news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old hat' reads as 'passé'; here it means a hat in old slang. A tile was once colloquial for a hat, especially a silk topper.
explanation.definitionFit: An old slang word for a hat, especially a top hat, is the same as the roofing piece.

clue.text: Contest what bad pupils are told to do?

definitions.text: what bad pupils are told to do?
definitions.meaning: naughty pupils are sent off to see the head teacher

explanation.surface: A school scene of misbehaving pupils being sent away.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits as 'head to Head': go to the headteacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A direct confrontation between two rivals is described with this hyphenated phrase.

clue.text: Is Lincoln entirely standing up queen?

parts.note: Abe is the short name of Abraham Lincoln

indicators.note: in a down entry this word is turned to read upwards

parts.note: all means entirely

explanation.surface: A question asking whether Abraham Lincoln, standing tall, is a queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Only ALL is reversed, giving LLA.
explanation.definitionFit: Isabella of Castile, who backed Columbus, is a famous royal of that name.

clue.text: Reliable types initially keen to crack emerging economies

indicators.note: to break into, so the letter goes within the economies group

parts.note: BRICS is the acronym for Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word keen is taken

explanation.surface: Dependable people are eager to break into developing markets.
explanation.definitionFit: A brick in colloquial British English is a dependable, good-hearted person, so the plural describes several such people.

clue.text: Part of church, perhaps eastern section

indicators.note: a section of the phrase perhaps eastern is taken, its letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: Describes an eastern part of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: The semicircular recess at the east end of a church holding the altar has this architectural name.

clue.text: Cryptically, how she runs home

parts.note: read cryptically, a wife (she) runs on after a house (home): the house word then the spouse word

explanation.surface: A description of a woman managing her household.
explanation.walkthrough: Straight, it describes a woman who runs a home; cryptically, 'she' (WIFE) runs after 'home' (HOUSE).
explanation.definitionFit: A woman whose main work is managing a household and family is given this traditional title.

clue.text: Bare land here

definitions.meaning: a runway or airstrip is where aircraft touch down

explanation.surface: An instruction that an empty patch of ground is the place to land.
explanation.definitionFit: Undressing is to strip, and a landing runway is an airstrip, often just called by the shorter word.

clue.text: Free to go through again, retaining key

indicators.note: keeping hold of, so the musical key sits inside

parts.note: to relive an experience is to go through it again
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: Someone free to repeat an experience while keeping a key.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve someone of a burden or duty frees them from it.

clue.text: Girl joining society left in first-class mess

parts.note: a deb, short for debutante, is a girl being introduced into high society

indicators.note: placed within the next word

parts.note: ace means excellent, first-class

explanation.surface: A debutante's arrival is spoiled when she is left in a first-class muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiasco or disastrous failure is a mess, a complete shambles.

clue.text: Tip: fill the gaps between 7

definitions.meaning: a sharp end, as of a pencil
7 down is bricks; builders fill joints between them with mortar

explanation.surface: Practical advice to a bricklayer about filling joints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' looks like advice heading the instruction, but it is a separate definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp end is a synonym for tip, and repairing mortar joints in brickwork is known in the building trade as pointing.

clue.text: Drool goes everywhere — he takes it on the chin

definitions.text: he takes it on the chin

indicators.note: spreading all over the place, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Saliva sprays about as someone is struck on the jaw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes' is part of the fodder, not a link: DROOL GOES rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who accepts defeat gracefully is said to take it on the chin, the mark of a gracious sportsman.

clue.text: Sack actor, high with cocaine, opening at the Abbey?

indicators.note: to sack a city is to wreck it, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: C is slang for cocaine

explanation.surface: Fire an actor who turns up high on drugs at the opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening at the Abbey' sounds like a premiere at Dublin's Abbey Theatre, but means a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointed doorway of the sort found in medieval abbeys is an example of this architectural shape.

clue.text: Bitterness to do with feeling one's ignored

parts.note: re means concerning, to do with

indicators.note: left out, so the letter for one is removed

parts.note: sentiment is feeling
I is the Roman numeral one; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Someone feels bitter at being overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Resentment is a sullen grievance, a synonym for bitterness.

clue.text: Users get authors to change one of their sources

indicators.note: the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Readers want writers to vary a reference work they use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'their' refers back to the authors: a word book writers consult.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Roget's book of synonyms is a standard reference that writers draw on for words.

clue.text: What pushy drivers do to gain entrance to estate

definitions.meaning: aggressive motorists drive too close behind the car in front
the rear lifting door of an estate car, the British name for a station wagon

explanation.surface: Aggressive drivers forcing their way into a housing estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'estate' is not land or housing but an estate car, British for station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: Driving too close behind another vehicle is the verb, and the hinged rear door of a hatchback or wagon is the noun.

clue.text: Local chairman's heading off

definitions.note: as a noun, a person living in the area

indicators.note: the head letter goes, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a president chairs a body; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A local chairman is leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' looks like an adjective but is the noun: a local person.
explanation.definitionFit: A local is someone living in the area, an inhabitant.

clue.text: Yen increased, provided one invested and got smarter?

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for the yen currency

indicators.note: put inside, as money is put into something

parts.note: upped means increased
if means provided
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A financial tale: the yen rose, someone invested and grew sharper.
explanation.definitionFit: A place gentrified for young professionals becomes smarter, so the past tense means made smart in that fashion.

clue.text: It crushes steel forged under pressure

indicators.note: in a down entry the anagram sits below the pressure letter

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for pressure in physics

indicators.note: metal forged is beaten into a new shape, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Steel shaped under pressure, then crushes.
explanation.definitionFit: The club-shaped tool used with a mortar pounds and grinds substances.

clue.text: He dresses Mother and Child

parts.note: ma is mother
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A man clothes a mother and her child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dresses' suggests clothing; a stonemason dresses stone, cutting and shaping it.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker who shapes and finishes stone, which is called dressing it, is a stoneworker.

clue.text: Hawk carries this weapon

definitions.meaning: a hawk is a plasterer's or bricklayer's square board for holding ... or plaster
a short-barrelled artillery piece firing at high angles

explanation.surface: A bird of prey carrying a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hawk' is not the bird but the builder's board, a flat square with a handle beneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Builders' binding paste is carried on a hawk, and the same word names a high-angle artillery piece.

clue.text: Turner cherished small silver dish

indicators.note: held close, so the name embraces the other letters

parts.note: Lana Turner was a Hollywood film star
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A beloved small silver serving dish made by a Turner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' suggests the painter J M W Turner or a woodturner; it is the actress Lana Turner.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian baked pasta layered with sauce is a classic dish.

clue.text: Story about male constituent of 21

indicators.note: surrounding, so the fib goes round the next letter

parts.note: a story is a lie, a fib

explanation.surface: A tale about a man being part of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is 21 down, mortar.
explanation.definitionFit: Traditional mortar is made from sand mixed with a calcium binder, quicklime, so it is an ingredient.

clue.text: Did nurse prepare Mark for weariness?

parts.note: to nurse a grudge is to bear it, so did nurse is bore
to do food is to prepare it
M is the abbreviation for mark, a former German currency

explanation.surface: A question whether a nurse readied Mark for exhaustion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a patient's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedium and the weary feeling of having nothing interesting to do are synonyms.

clue.text: Run off some cloth from old mill town on leaving

indicators.note: the word on departs from the town's name

parts.words: some cloth from old mill town
parts.note: Bolton, a Lancashire cotton-mill town
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone flees with cloth from a mill town.
explanation.walkthrough: Bolton is a former cotton-mill town in Lancashire, England. A bolt is also a roll of cloth, a hint woven into the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To flee suddenly or abscond is a synonym for running off.

clue.text: Fine chimney in Glasgow backs onto court

indicators.note: goes backwards, so the Scots word is read in reverse

parts.note: lum is Scots for a chimney

explanation.surface: A smart Glasgow chimney backing onto a courtyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' looks like an adjective but is the verb or noun: a penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: A mulct is a formal word for a monetary penalty, used as noun or verb.

clue.text: Pass priest eating Northern Irish food

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

indicators.note: taking in, so the clergyman's title swallows the letter

parts.note: a canon is a clergyman

explanation.surface: A priest passes on a dish while eating something Northern Irish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Northern Irish' reads as one phrase; it splits into N and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This mash of potato with cabbage or kale is a traditional dish of Ireland.
